To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the energy exchange between the conduction electrons in a metal and magnetic impurities in the absence of a magnetic field occurs through the exchange interaction, and that in a magnetic field, the energy exchange is mediated by the spin-flip scattering.
the electron dephases faster when it scatters from a magnetic impurity, but the Zeeman splitting slows down the dephasing.
the magnetic field reduces the dephasing of the electronic wave functions and increases the conductance fluctuations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electron transport in the presence of spin-flip scattering by magnetic impurities.
the electron transport in disordered conductors with magnetic impurities.
the effect of magnetic field and impurities on the electron energy and phase relaxation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
magnetic impurities in the presence of a magnetic field can be a source of electron energy relaxation and dephasing.
the magnetic impurity effect on the inelastic processes in metals has not been established yet.
the magnetic impurities are not the dominant source for the dephasing of the electronic states in the diffusive metallic systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the electron-electron interaction in the presence of a strong magnetic field leads to a new type of the electron-electron collision integral, which is different from the one in the absence of a magnetic field.
the magnetic impurities are not only the source for the electron dephrasing, but also the source for the energy relaxation of the electrons.
the electron dephases on magnetic impurities in two ways: (i) the magnetic impurity mediates energy exchange between electrons, and (ii) the magnetic field reduces the electron dephase rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electron energy relaxation rate is proportional to T2, where T is the temperature, while the dephasing rate is proportional to the electron temperature, which is proportional to T1/2.
magnetic impurities can be used to control electron dephasing and to tune the strength of the electron interference effects in conductors.
the effect of the magnetic impurity spin is much stronger than that of the orbital magnetic moment.
